kevin: Heads up — since the runtime v2.3.1 canary (deployed ~10:12) we're seeing widespread gaps in token-level latency metrics and a simultaneous spike in per-route p95 for text-generation routes. StatsD emitter logs show repeated errors: `udp: write: message too long` and the OTel traces for those requests are missing token-level timing spans. KV-cache hit ratio on chat-prod dropped from ~98% -> ~83% around the same time. Repro logs/snippet below.

kevin: ```
ERROR emitter/statsd.go:142: failed to send metric: write udp 10.0.0.3:0->10.0.0.5:8125: message too long
WARN runtime/metrics_collector.go:87: missing token_timing span for request id=abc123
KV Cache stats: hits=83, misses=17, entries=1.2M
Batching window: continuous-batch enabled, max_delay_ms=8
Kernel selector: fused-attn-v2 selected for causal/seq<=128
```

maria: Thx. Two likely suspects off the top of my head: the new kernel selection rule that prefers fused-attn-v2 for short seqs, and the continuous batching config change that reduced the batching delay. Both could interact badly with KV cache behavior and StatsD emitter packetization.

aj: Quick notes from profiling: after v2.3.1 we see a ~20% regression in per-token latency for single-stream chat workloads. Flamegraphs show increased memcpy + kernel launch overhead in fused-attn-v2 path when KV cache is hit (lots of small KV loads). The old kernel had more compute but fewer small copies.

aj: Example from perf run: `avg_token_ms: before=2.1ms after=2.6ms (single stream, kv-hit)`

sam: Regarding metrics dropouts, ops-bot shows StatsD buffer flush size 512KB. With multiple metrics (token-level + per-token breakdown every token), the UDP payload exceeded MTU occasionally and was dropped. We should either switch to TCP/OTel exporter for token-level metrics or compress/batch differently.

lina: Can we get a quick diff of what changed in emitter config in the deploy? I think someone tuned down emitter batching to reduce data-lag last quarter. If continuous-batch is emitting per-token counters, payloads explode.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary roll detected for runtime-service v2.3.1 -> action: paused canary in us-west-2; rolled back to v2.3.0 in canary cohort (2024-03-16T10:23:41Z).

kevin: Rollback helps restore metrics for now (we're seeing token timing reappear), but we still have regression root causes to fix before re-rolling. Key follow-ups: 
- fix kernel selector heuristics so fused-attn-v2 isn't chosen when KV-cache heavy / batch_size==1 patterns are detected
- revisit continuous-batch config for token-level metrics emission (avoid per-token UDP payload explosion)
- backfill missing token-level metrics for 10:12-10:23 window using OTel traces (if traces exist) or request logs otherwise
- add improved exporter error telemetry (surface `message too long` counts in infra dashboards)

maria: For kernel selector, propose quick patch: add conditional that forces legacy-attn path when (kv_hit_rate > 90% AND avg_batch_size < 2). That should be low-risk and cover chat-heavy patterns. I'll draft.

aj: I'll run microbench on a small 1-stream kv-hit workload with both kernels + memcpy tracing (nvprof + custom tracer) to validate. Expect to have numbers in ~45m.

sam: I'll own the backfill. Plan: 1) query OTel span DB for token timing spans between 1710703920 and 1710705180, 2) if missing, reconstruct token timings from request trace logs using per-token micro-timings from the runtime traces, 3) emit backfill metrics to metrics-store via internal backfill job (id: backfill-1710704821). ETA 3h.

lina: I'll audit emitter config and bump message batching to 256KB or enable fallbacks to TCP for burst windows. Will open PR for config rollback or opt-in compression.

kevin: ops-bot, can you create a Grafana alert for `statsd.emitter.errors > 0` and attach last 6 hours window and a panel for `token_latency_per_token` missing-series? We need on-call visibility.

ops-bot: alert created: `EMITTER_ERRORS_NONZERO` -> sev=page, threshold=1, channels=#eng-sre,#oncall. Grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/org/redwood/d/abcd/token-latency-breakdown (shared).

maria: Also let's keep a perf-protection gate: if kernel selector changes increase memcpy or kernel-launch overhead by >10% for our chat profile, block rollout. I'll file a small CI perf test that runs the single-stream kv-hit profile on each canary commit.

aj: FYI my initial perf run shows memcpy time up 22% and kernel-launch up 8% on fused-attn-v2 for our profile. Putting numbers in the ticket.

kevin: Good. Owners: maria (kernel selector patch), aj (profiling + perf CI), sam (backfill job), lina (emitter config), ops-bot (alert + dashboard). Please update the related GH issues and ping when PRs ready.

maria: Draft PR #4521 coming in ~30m for the selector guard.

sam: Backfill job started: job=backfill-1710704821, will post progress.

kevin: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the backfill and perf CI runs. :thumbsup:

sam: backfill update (10m): OTel DB has ~60% of token spans for the window, remaining requests reconstructed from runtime traces. Emitted ~98% of missing token-level metrics so dashboards look mostly recovered.

kevin: Awesome — leaving this thread open until CI + selector patch merged and canary is re-rolled safely.
